core.title: Physics‐Informed Multisource Domain Transfer Learning for Fatigue Life Prediction of IN718 Alloy
core.venue: Fatigue & Fracture of Engineering Materials & Structures
core.abstract: ABSTRACT A physics‐informed multisource domain transfer learning (PITL) prediction model was proposed to predict fatigue life of IN718 superalloy under complex conditions, which faced sparse data and complex mechanism challenges. The model effectively integrates physical prior knowledge and transfer learning algorithms widely used in current fatigue research and engineering fields, such as equivalent effect variable model, Manson–Coffin model, and other physical information, as well as low‐cycle fatigue hysteresis‐loop characteristic information, based on its architecture. It effectively solves the problem of learning and utilizing multisource data in fatigue testing and achieves accurate prediction of fatigue life under different strain‐ratio loading conditions based on known fatigue loading conditions. And then, the effects of different model combinations, multisource transfer patterns, and multisource data size on the accuracy of target domain life prediction are systematically explored under four strain ratios loading condition. The results show that the PITL model incorporating physical information exhibits higher prediction accuracy and robustness than the basic transfer learning model. Its predictive performance depends on the model combinations, the transfer patterns, and the amount of data in the source domain.

core.title: Research on the application framework of multi-agent technology-driven failure analysis for industrial products
core.abstract: Accurate failure analysis in intelligent supercharging stations is critical for operational safety and efficiency. However, traditional methods suffer from poor cross-condition adaptability, limited few-shot learning capability, and insufficient cross-model generalization. This paper proposes a Multi-Agent Failure Analysis Execution System (FAES), which synergistically integrates a Multimodal Workbench, an Intelligence Hub, and a modular agent cluster. The Multimodal Workbench fuses heterogeneous sensor data (voltage, current, temperature, acoustic) through a progressive three-level fusion strategy with cross-modal attention and Dempster-Shafer evidence theory. The Intelligence Hub formulates task allocation as a constrained optimization problem, which is relaxed to a differentiable softmax routing mechanism. This enables real-time, load-aware scheduling. A fine-tuned large language model (Qwen3-Omni) provides domain-adaptive diagnostic reasoning through closed-loop reinforcement learning from human feedback. Extensive experiments on real-world charging station data demonstrate that FAES achieves 83.2% diagnostic accuracy under few-shot cross-dataset transfer-a 15.8 percentage point improvement over training from scratch and reduces average response time by 42.9% (from 4.2 s to 2.4 s) via dynamic multi-agent scheduling. Ablation studies quantify the contribution of each component, while hallucination analysis confirms a low rate of just 0.4%. These results establish FAES as an explainable, generalizable solution for industrial fault diagnosis, filling a critical gap in the application of LLM-based multi-agent collaboration to charging station maintenance.

core.title: Operational Risks and AI Bias in LLM-Based Agentic Systems for a Process Plant: Electric Motor Operations Case Study (Oil & Gas)
core.abstract: The rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs) has encouraged many industries to explore Agentic AI. Earlier AI tools were used mainly for data analysis and information retrieval. Newer systems can carry out a sequence of related tasks, combine information from several engineering sources and prepare recommendations with relatively limited user input. These capabilities can support document review, procurement quality, maintenance planning, commissioning and operational troubleshooting. However, they also bring risks that are not normally associated with conventional engineering software. Because the output is probabilistic, a recommendation may be influenced by missing technical information, incomplete operating context, biased source material or incorrect interpretation of safety-critical requirements. It may still appear convincing even when its engineering basis is weak. Electric motors are used throughout oil and gas facilities and are essential to the operation of pumps, compressors, fans, cooling systems and other plant equipment. A motor failure can interrupt production and, in some cases, affect the safety or reliability of the wider process. Decisions relating to motor protection, alarms, equipment condition, commissioning, fault diagnosis and maintenance therefore require sound engineering judgement, supported by approved protection settings, operating history, OEM guidance and relevant international standards. This makes electric motors a practical case for examining the use of LLM-based Agentic AI in a safety-critical engineering environment. The paper considers a series of representative motor scenarios covering design review, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), commissioning, operational troubleshooting, predictive maintenance, alarm assessment and root cause analysis. The findings show that prediction accuracy and model confidence alone do not establish whether an AI recommendation is safe or technically reliable. That judgement depends on the quality of the available evidence, the completeness of the operating context, compliance with applicable standards and protection philosophy, and verification by a qualified engineer. To manage these risks, the paper introduces the Engineering Trustworthiness Assurance Framework (ETAF). It brings the main checks into one process, starting with the quality of the available engineering information and ending with the approval of the final recommendation. ETAF includes the Engineering AI Assurance Pyramid (EAAP), the Operational AI Risk Propagation Model (OARPM) and the AI Engineering Governance Matrix (AEGM). It also uses three assessment measures: the Engineering Trustworthiness Score (ETS), AI Recommendation Criticality Level (ARCL) and Engineering Confidence Index (ECI). These are proposed as practical, illustrative tools that organisations can adapt when introducing LLM-assisted decision support in safety-critical engineering work. Although the representative scenarios are based on electric motor operations, the proposed framework is applicable to other classes of rotating equipment deployed throughout upstream, midstream, and downstream oil and gas facilities. The paper contributes a practical engineering governance approach that complements existing AI assurance initiatives by emphasizing engineering trustworthiness, protection philosophy, operational accountability, and responsible human oversight during the deployment of Agentic AI systems.

core.title: A Layered View of LLM Support in Underwater Robotics
core.abstract: This extended abstract discusses a specific and, in our experience, practically relevant role for large language models (LLMs) in underwater robotics. Our main premise is that, in underwater fielding missions, the immediate difficulty is often not the synthesis of new low-level control laws, but the operation of complex robotic systems under limited communications, partial observability, and expensive field time. In particular, a significant fraction of the effort during sea trials is devoted to fault diagnosis, telemetry interpretation, mission adjustment, and coordination across heterogeneous assets and operators. We argue that LLMs may be useful at this higher operational level, especially when grounded in structured vehicle state, alarms, logs, mission context, and existing planning or validation tools. At the same time, current limitations in grounding, consistency, and causal reasoning make these systems lack the predictability required to guarantee direct control, especially in real-world critical applications, although we do not exclude a future evolution in this direction. This viewpoint suggests a layered architecture in which conventional autonomy remains responsible for control, perception, estimation, and validated mission execution, whereas LLM-based modules serve as an additional support layer for debugging, operator interaction, constrained replanning support, orchestration, and post-mission analysis.

core.title: Equipment Reliability DNA: Decoding Failure Patterns with eDNA Analytics
core.abstract: Reliable failure data is the starting point for practical reliability engineering in oil and gas operations. In many assets, however, the most useful failure information is recorded in free-text maintenance work-order narratives rather than in consistently populated structured fields. As a result, historical records are difficult to use directly for Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM), Root Cause Analysis (RCA), Reliability, Availability, and Maintainability (RAM) studies, bad-actor analysis, and predictive-maintenance development. Before the Equipment Data and Analysis (eDNA) platform was introduced, it was estimated that approximately 80% of maintenance failure records were not immediately suitable for reliability analysis because the failure descriptions and classification fields were incomplete, inconsistent, or dependent on local terminology. Reliability engineers therefore had to read work orders manually, interpret the maintenance narrative, and map each event to an ISO 14224-aligned failure taxonomy. This work consumed engineering time and was difficult to scale across the volume of corrective-maintenance transactions generated by multiple offshore and onshore assets. PTTEP developed eDNA to convert this unstructured maintenance history into reviewable, standardized reliability data. The platform combines SAP maintenance work orders, equipment master data, and operating-context information with a Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) workflow based on Large Language Models (LLMs). The workflow interprets narrative text, proposes failure mode, failure mechanism, failed part, action, and severity classifications aligned with ISO 14224, and routes the output through reliability-engineer validation. SAP, and Plant Data Management System are integrated through a centralized cloud data lake, with results are visualized through Power BI dashboards and Asset Performance Management (APM) tools. Across nine operating assets, eDNA has processed multi-year historical failure records and has materially reduced manual data-cleansing effort. The model currently reports more than 65% classification accuracy and continues to improve through engineering feedback and prompt refinement. More importantly, eDNA has created a common MTBF/MTTR baseline for cross-asset benchmarking, bad-actor identification, and future predictive-maintenance development. This paper describes the business problem, data workflow, AI classification approach, validation process, deployment results, and lessons learned from the eDNA implementation.

core.title: A Large Language Model-based Generative Artificial Intelligence and hybrid machine learning framework for prediction and inverse design of jute fiber concrete
core.abstract: The construction industry requires sustainable alternatives to conventional concrete to reduce environmental impacts while maintaining structural performance. Jute fiber concrete (JFC) is a promising low-carbon material; however, optimizing its mechanical properties is challenging because of complex nonlinear interactions among fiber characteristics and mix-design parameters. This study proposes an integrated framework combining Generative Artificial Intelligence (GEN-AI) with Decision Tree Boosting (DT-Boosting), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and GPR enhanced with Bayesian Optimization (GPR-BO) to predict and optimize JFC mechanical properties. An experimental dataset containing six input variables were expanded using a Large Language Model-based GEN-AI approach and validated through distribution analysis, boxplot comparisons, and Kendall correlation analysis. GPR-based models significantly outperformed DT-Boosting, reducing prediction errors by approximately 40–50%. The GPR-BO achieved the most consistent performance, with testing R 2 values of 0.9242 for compressive strength and 0.9682 for tensile strength. However, the SHAP and Partial Dependence Plot analyses identified jute fiber volume fraction and fiber content as the most influential parameters, while the water–cement ratio exhibited a strong negative effect. Probabilistic validation confirmed accurate reproduction of strength distributions. Furthermore, integrating GPR-BO with NSGA-II enabled inverse mix design, automatically generating optimized JFC mixtures satisfying user-defined mechanical performance requirements. The optimization employed six mix-design decision variables and minimized both normalized prediction error and fiber volume fraction to identify Pareto-optimal solutions. The resulting framework extends forward prediction to practical inverse design, reducing trial-and-error experimentation and material waste while supporting resource-efficient, performance-based, and sustainable concrete mix development for engineering applications.

article.lead: 黄麻纤维混凝土如何兼顾低碳潜力与力学性能？这项研究将大语言模型数据扩增、强度预测与配合比逆向设计串联起来，阅读价值在于理解模型如何从“预测材料性能”走向“按性能要求寻找配方”。

sections.title: 黄麻纤维混凝土的难点在于非线性配比关系
paragraphs: 建筑业需要降低环境影响，同时维持材料的结构性能。摘要将黄麻纤维混凝土（JFC）视为一种有潜力的低碳材料，但纤维特征与配合比参数之间存在复杂的非线性相互作用，使力学性能优化并不容易。研究围绕这一问题，将性能预测与配合比优化纳入同一框架。

sections.title: 从生成式数据扩增到多目标逆向设计
paragraphs: 研究以包含六个输入变量的实验数据集为基础，利用大语言模型驱动的生成式人工智能扩增数据，并通过分布分析、箱线图比较和Kendall相关分析进行核验。随后采用决策树提升（DT-Boosting）、高斯过程回归（GPR）及贝叶斯优化增强的GPR（GPR-BO）预测力学性能。
研究还利用SHAP与部分依赖图分析参数影响，并将GPR-BO与NSGA-II结合开展逆向配合比设计。优化涉及六个配合比决策变量，以同时最小化归一化预测误差和纤维体积分数为目标，寻找满足用户力学性能要求的Pareto最优解。

sections.title: GPR预测占优，纤维参数影响突出
paragraphs: 摘要报告，GPR类模型优于DT-Boosting，预测误差降低约40–50%。其中，GPR-BO表现最为稳定，抗压强度和抗拉强度的测试集R²分别为0.9242和0.9682。摘要还报告，概率验证能够准确复现强度分布。
解释性分析识别出黄麻纤维体积分数与纤维含量是影响最大的参数，而水灰比呈现较强的负向影响。逆向设计部分则报告，框架能够自动生成满足用户指定力学性能要求的优化配合比，将正向强度预测进一步连接到配方搜索。

sections.title: 黄麻纤维混凝土的难点在于非线性配比关系
paragraphs: 建筑业需要降低环境影响，同时维持材料的结构性能。摘要将黄麻纤维混凝土（JFC）视为一种有潜力的低碳材料，但纤维特征与配合比参数之间存在复杂的非线性相互作用，使力学性能优化并不容易。研究围绕这一问题，将性能预测与配合比优化纳入同一框架。

sections.title: 从生成式数据扩增到多目标逆向设计

研究还利用SHAP与部分依赖图分析参数影响，并将GPR-BO与NSGA-II结合开展逆向配合比设计。优化涉及六个配合比决策变量，以同时最小化归一化预测误差和纤维体积分数为目标，寻找满足用户力学性能要求的Pareto最优解。

papers.title: Physics‐Informed Multisource Domain Transfer Learning for Fatigue Life Prediction of IN718 Alloy
papers.venue: Fatigue & Fracture of Engineering Materials & Structures
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT A physics‐informed multisource domain transfer learning (PITL) prediction model was proposed to predict fatigue life of IN718 superalloy under complex conditions, which faced sparse data and complex mechanism challenges. The model effectively integrates physical prior knowledge and transfer learning algorithms widely used in current fatigue research and engineering fields, such as equivalent effect variable model, Manson–Coffin model, and other physical information, as well as low‐cycle fatigue hysteresis‐loop characteristic information, based on its architecture. It effectively solves the problem of learning and utilizing multisource data in fatigue testing and achieves accurate prediction of fatigue life under different strain‐ratio loading conditions based on known fatigue loading conditions. And then, the effects of different model combinations, multisource transfer patterns, and multisource data size on the accuracy of target domain life prediction are systematically explored under four strain ratios loading condition. The results show that the PITL model incorporating physical information exhibits higher prediction accuracy and robustness than the basic transfer learning model. Its predictive performance depends on the model combinations, the transfer patterns, and the amount of data in the source domain.

papers.title: Research on the application framework of multi-agent technology-driven failure analysis for industrial products
papers.abstract: Accurate failure analysis in intelligent supercharging stations is critical for operational safety and efficiency. However, traditional methods suffer from poor cross-condition adaptability, limited few-shot learning capability, and insufficient cross-model generalization. This paper proposes a Multi-Agent Failure Analysis Execution System (FAES), which synergistically integrates a Multimodal Workbench, an Intelligence Hub, and a modular agent cluster. The Multimodal Workbench fuses heterogeneous sensor data (voltage, current, temperature, acoustic) through a progressive three-level fusion strategy with cross-modal attention and Dempster-Shafer evidence theory. The Intelligence Hub formulates task allocation as a constrained optimization problem, which is relaxed to a differentiable softmax routing mechanism. This enables real-time, load-aware scheduling. A fine-tuned large language model (Qwen3-Omni) provides domain-adaptive diagnostic reasoning through closed-loop reinforcement learning from human feedback. Extensive experiments on real-world charging station data demonstrate that FAES achieves 83.2% diagnostic accuracy under few-shot cross-dataset transfer-a 15.8 percentage point improvement over training from scratch and reduces average response time by 42.9% (from 4.2 s to 2.4 s) via dynamic multi-agent scheduling. Ablation studies quantify the contribution of each component, while hallucination analysis confirms a low rate of just 0.4%. These results establish FAES as an explainable, generalizable solution for industrial fault diagnosis, filling a critical gap in the application of LLM-based multi-agent collaboration to charging station maintenance.

papers.title: Operational Risks and AI Bias in LLM-Based Agentic Systems for a Process Plant: Electric Motor Operations Case Study (Oil & Gas)
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs) has encouraged many industries to explore Agentic AI. Earlier AI tools were used mainly for data analysis and information retrieval. Newer systems can carry out a sequence of related tasks, combine information from several engineering sources and prepare recommendations with relatively limited user input. These capabilities can support document review, procurement quality, maintenance planning, commissioning and operational troubleshooting. However, they also bring risks that are not normally associated with conventional engineering software. Because the output is probabilistic, a recommendation may be influenced by missing technical information, incomplete operating context, biased source material or incorrect interpretation of safety-critical requirements. It may still appear convincing even when its engineering basis is weak. Electric motors are used throughout oil and gas facilities and are essential to the operation of pumps, compressors, fans, cooling systems and other plant equipment. A motor failure can interrupt production and, in some cases, affect the safety or reliability of the wider process. Decisions relating to motor protection, alarms, equipment condition, commissioning, fault diagnosis and maintenance therefore require sound engineering judgement, supported by approved protection settings, operating history, OEM guidance and relevant international standards. This makes electric motors a practical case for examining the use of LLM-based Agentic AI in a safety-critical engineering environment. The paper considers a series of representative motor scenarios covering design review, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), commissioning, operational troubleshooting, predictive maintenance, alarm assessment and root cause analysis. The findings show that prediction accuracy and model confidence alone do not establish whether an AI recommendation is safe or technically reliable. That judgement depends on the quality of the available evidence, the completeness of the operating context, compliance with applicable standards and protection philosophy, and verification by a qualified engineer. To manage these risks, the paper introduces the Engineering Trustworthiness Assurance Framework (ETAF). It brings the main checks into one process, starting with the quality of the available engineering information and ending with the approval of the final recommendation. ETAF includes the Engineering AI Assurance Pyramid (EAAP), the Operational AI Risk Propagation Model (OARPM) and the AI Engineering Governance Matrix (AEGM). It also uses three assessment measures: the Engineering Trustworthiness Score (ETS), AI Recommendation Criticality Level (ARCL) and Engineering Confidence Index (ECI). These are proposed as practical, illustrative tools that organisations can adapt when introducing LLM-assisted decision support in safety-critical engineering work. Although the representative scenarios are based on electric motor operations, the proposed framework is applicable to other classes of rotating equipment deployed throughout upstream, midstream, and downstream oil and gas facilities. The paper contributes a practical engineering governance approach that complements existing AI assurance initiatives by emphasizing engineering trustworthiness, protection philosophy, operational accountability, and responsible human oversight during the deployment of Agentic AI systems.

papers.title: A Layered View of LLM Support in Underwater Robotics
papers.abstract: This extended abstract discusses a specific and, in our experience, practically relevant role for large language models (LLMs) in underwater robotics. Our main premise is that, in underwater fielding missions, the immediate difficulty is often not the synthesis of new low-level control laws, but the operation of complex robotic systems under limited communications, partial observability, and expensive field time. In particular, a significant fraction of the effort during sea trials is devoted to fault diagnosis, telemetry interpretation, mission adjustment, and coordination across heterogeneous assets and operators. We argue that LLMs may be useful at this higher operational level, especially when grounded in structured vehicle state, alarms, logs, mission context, and existing planning or validation tools. At the same time, current limitations in grounding, consistency, and causal reasoning make these systems lack the predictability required to guarantee direct control, especially in real-world critical applications, although we do not exclude a future evolution in this direction. This viewpoint suggests a layered architecture in which conventional autonomy remains responsible for control, perception, estimation, and validated mission execution, whereas LLM-based modules serve as an additional support layer for debugging, operator interaction, constrained replanning support, orchestration, and post-mission analysis.

papers.title: Equipment Reliability DNA: Decoding Failure Patterns with eDNA Analytics
papers.abstract: Reliable failure data is the starting point for practical reliability engineering in oil and gas operations. In many assets, however, the most useful failure information is recorded in free-text maintenance work-order narratives rather than in consistently populated structured fields. As a result, historical records are difficult to use directly for Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM), Root Cause Analysis (RCA), Reliability, Availability, and Maintainability (RAM) studies, bad-actor analysis, and predictive-maintenance development. Before the Equipment Data and Analysis (eDNA) platform was introduced, it was estimated that approximately 80% of maintenance failure records were not immediately suitable for reliability analysis because the failure descriptions and classification fields were incomplete, inconsistent, or dependent on local terminology. Reliability engineers therefore had to read work orders manually, interpret the maintenance narrative, and map each event to an ISO 14224-aligned failure taxonomy. This work consumed engineering time and was difficult to scale across the volume of corrective-maintenance transactions generated by multiple offshore and onshore assets. PTTEP developed eDNA to convert this unstructured maintenance history into reviewable, standardized reliability data. The platform combines SAP maintenance work orders, equipment master data, and operating-context information with a Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) workflow based on Large Language Models (LLMs). The workflow interprets narrative text, proposes failure mode, failure mechanism, failed part, action, and severity classifications aligned with ISO 14224, and routes the output through reliability-engineer validation. papers.abstract: The construction industry requires sustainable alternatives to conventional concrete to reduce environmental impacts while maintaining structural performance. Jute fiber concrete (JFC) is a promising low-carbon material; however, optimizing its mechanical properties is challenging because of complex nonlinear interactions among fiber characteristics and mix-design parameters. This study proposes an integrated framework combining Generative Artificial Intelligence (GEN-AI) with Decision Tree Boosting (DT-Boosting), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and GPR enhanced with Bayesian Optimization (GPR-BO) to predict and optimize JFC mechanical properties. An experimental dataset containing six input variables were expanded using a Large Language Model-based GEN-AI approach and validated through distribution analysis, boxplot comparisons, and Kendall correlation analysis. GPR-based models significantly outperformed DT-Boosting, reducing prediction errors by approximately 40–50%. The GPR-BO achieved the most consistent performance, with testing R 2 values of 0.9242 for compressive strength and 0.9682 for tensile strength. Probabilistic validation confirmed accurate reproduction of strength distributions. Furthermore, integrating GPR-BO with NSGA-II enabled inverse mix design, automatically generating optimized JFC mixtures satisfying user-defined mechanical performance requirements. The optimization employed six mix-design decision variables and minimized both normalized prediction error and fiber volume fraction to identify Pareto-optimal solutions. article.lead: 黄麻纤维混凝土如何兼顾低碳潜力与力学性能？这项研究将大语言模型数据扩增、强度预测与配合比逆向设计串联起来，阅读价值在于理解模型如何从“预测材料性能”走向“按性能要求寻找配方”。

sections.title: 黄麻纤维混凝土的难点在于非线性配比关系
paragraphs: 建筑业需要降低环境影响，同时维持材料的结构性能。摘要将黄麻纤维混凝土（JFC）视为一种有潜力的低碳材料，但纤维特征与配合比参数之间存在复杂的非线性相互作用，使力学性能优化并不容易。研究围绕这一问题，将性能预测与配合比优化纳入同一框架。

sections.title: 从生成式数据扩增到多目标逆向设计
paragraphs: 研究以包含六个输入变量的实验数据集为基础，利用大语言模型驱动的生成式人工智能扩增数据，并通过分布分析、箱线图比较和Kendall相关分析进行核验。随后采用决策树提升（DT-Boosting）、高斯过程回归（GPR）及贝叶斯优化增强的GPR（GPR-BO）预测力学性能。
研究还利用SHAP与部分依赖图分析参数影响，并将GPR-BO与NSGA-II结合开展逆向配合比设计。优化涉及六个配合比决策变量，以同时最小化归一化预测误差和纤维体积分数为目标，寻找满足用户力学性能要求的Pareto最优解。

sections.title: GPR预测占优，纤维参数影响突出
paragraphs: 摘要报告，GPR类模型优于DT-Boosting，预测误差降低约40–50%。其中，GPR-BO表现最为稳定，抗压强度和抗拉强度的测试集R²分别为0.9242和0.9682。摘要还报告，概率验证能够准确复现强度分布。
解释性分析识别出黄麻纤维体积分数与纤维含量是影响最大的参数，而水灰比呈现较强的负向影响。逆向设计部分则报告，框架能够自动生成满足用户指定力学性能要求的优化配合比，将正向强度预测进一步连接到配方搜索。

sections.title: 预测指标之外，验证边界仍需查阅全文
paragraphs: 仅凭本次摘要，无法判断原始实验样本量、扩增规模、训练测试划分，以及生成数据如何参与评估；扩增数据也不能视为新增的独立实验样本。误差降低所对应的具体指标、模型比较设置和统计检验细节同样未在摘要中展开。
摘要未交代逆向设计配方的独立制备验证范围，也不足以判断跨材料来源或配比范围的泛化能力。减少试错与材料浪费是作者强调的应用价值，但摘要未给出相应量化结果，不能据此认定其工程节约效果已经得到充分验证。

sections.title: 阅读启发：区分配方可预测与配方可实现
paragraphs: 阅读启发：这项工作的关注点不仅是预测精度，还包括如何把性能要求转化为配方候选。进一步阅读时，值得核对生成数据与独立测试的关系、Pareto解的取舍方式，以及候选配方是否获得独立实验支持，从而区分模型中的目标满足与实际材料性能达标。
